items.label: A
items.critique: Short and plain, close to Nox, but two of three lines are quest hooks (kidnapped daughter, stolen bell) and the weather filler is a tidy contrast beat.

items.label: B
items.critique: Generic, slightly wordy travel warnings ('preying on the trade routes', 'more brazen') with masked places and a 'Young [Class]!' address: campaign gossip.

items.label: C
items.critique: Terse, almost random one-liners ('Beware of the rising undead.'), a tavern joke and a shop tip: the unpolished townsfolk filler of the original.

items.label: D
items.critique: The toad-student gag is good and Nox-like, but every line is engineered to point at a quest, and titles (the Archivist, Master [Person]) replace names.

items.label: E
items.critique: Two crisp hooks with a reward promise and a busy-passerby line; the structure (hook, hook, brush-off) is too purposeful.

items.label: F
items.critique: Meandering gossip with 'Hello.' openers, the 'old goat' jab and a self-undercutting 'who spreads these insane rumors': Westwood's voice.

items.label: G
items.critique: A joke line (paid in turnips) followed by two hooks with stakes and reward ('He'll pay well'); neat and on-message in the way new texts are.

items.label: H
items.critique: Lowercase 'ogres', '--' dash, 'Well good luck to ya' and the deadpan 'Maybe we shouldn't have built so close to the ogre village' are the campaign's humour.

items.label: I
items.critique: Directions and civic news in a flat, slightly clunky register ('Breakdowns in the city have become more frequent'); points the player around, not at quests.

items.label: J
items.critique: Complaint gag, then a monster hook and a missing-scout hook naming 'the Captain': the same hook-heavy, titled-NPC pattern.

tells: New rumour sets are built as quest hooks: two of three lines name a monster, a victim or stolen thing, and often a reward. Westwood's townsfolk mostly give vague warnings, directions or idle gossip.
New texts name NPCs by title (the Captain, the Foreman, the Archivist, the Mayor) where Westwood uses masked names and places.
A neat recurring shape in new sets: one comic complaint or brush-off plus two hooks. Westwood's lines are uneven in length and purpose.
Westwood's humour is deadpan and self-undercutting (rumour-mongers doubting rumours, building next to ogres); new humour is a one-off quip (turnips, toad student, snow in the soup).
Westwood shows small roughness: 'Hello.' openers, lowercase monster names, '--', wordy stock phrasing ('strange and disturbing stories'); new lines are cleaner and tighter.
